Former Packers players criticized Rodgers for attacking McCarthy publicly and putting his ex-Steelers teammates in an uncomfortable position
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 26, 2026
                            
                    at
    12:48 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Aaron Rodgers' recent comments about Mike McCarthy have drawn the ire of some of his former Green Bay Packers teammates. Former Packers offensive lineman T.J. Lang and former Packers receivers James Jones and Greg Jennings have publicly denounced Rodgers' treatment of McCarthy while taking their former coach's side following a chaotic 48-hour period in Pittsburgh. Rodgers scorched McCarthy on "The Pat McAfee Show" on Wednesday, accusing his now-former coach of falling asleep at meetings, being late or absent from other meetings, not watching film in a timely manner and not developing a rapport with some of his players, especially the team's defensive players. Rodgers was benched after giving McCarthy an ultimatum: relinquish play-calling duties or release him. McCarthy benched Rodgers, and the Steelers released him after Rodgers publicly criticized McCarthy. "I think it's despicable," Lang said on 97.1 The Ticket in Detroit. "I think that Aaron Rodgers just became everything that he has bitched about and moaned about over the last 10 years with former coaches, former teammates airing grievances out, giving opinions out in the media. He has blacklisted, I don't know how many former teammates from just simple comments telling the truth because he just he was sick of it."Lang, who spent eight seasons with Rodgers and McCarthy in Green Bay, said that he is in a group chat with several former Packers who share his sentiment on the situation. 
"I think it's just completely unnecessary," he said. "I think it's victim mentality." 
Jones, who also spent eight seasons with Rodgers and McCarthy in Green Bay, said he, too, is in a group text with former Packers teammates who don't agree with Rodgers' handling of McCarthy. "How do you jump on Pat McAfee's show and say all this? Come on, man," Jones said on the Speakeasy podcast. "My text thread is full of texts and group chats with a lot of my teammates right now, and none are on 12's side, especially the ones that know Mike."  
Jennings, who spent seven seasons in Green Bay and caught two touchdowns in the Packers' Super Bowl win over the Steelers, called Rodgers' decision to publicly air his grievances with McCarthy "distasteful." Jennings also criticized Rodgers for putting his former teammates in Pittsburgh in an awkward situation. "If you truly cared about more than just yourself, then you don't do this to everybody in that locker room that you just called brothers," Jennings said on "First Thing First." "They are playing for something. You are no longer playing for anything." 
The general consensus among Rodgers' former Packers teammates is that Rodgers should have handled the situation behind closed doors, even if some of his accusations about McCarthy are true. 
"I don't even care if it's the truth," Jones said. "Have the conversation with Mike in there. This is not something you go to the media bashing somebody. I would not do this to people that I love."

The Commanders stay hot. Pick: Commanders 30, Cardinals 19Seattle Seahawks at San Francisco 49ers (-3.5)Sunday, 4:25 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free)The 49ers have the best record in the NFC and seem to be cruising to the division title. Look for a lower-scoring game in the second division game between the two — the 49ers won the first — and San Francisco will win it late.
Pick: 49ers 21, Seahawks 17Las Vegas Raiders at Cleveland Browns (-4.5) Sunday, 8:20 p.m. on NBC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free)This has been flexed to prime time because the Browns would be a playoff team right now. So what gives? I think the Tampa Bay defense will play well here and the Bucs will run it right at Carolina to win it like they did in the first meeting.Pick: Bucs 23, Panthers 17 Chicago Bears at Detroit Lions (+2.5)Thursday, 1 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+)This should be an offensive show. The Bears defense has played well since getting Jeffrey Simmons in a trade, but they won't stop the Lions here. Look for a lot of points with the home team getting the victory on Thanksgiving.

body:
Rooney said the Steelers could not tolerate Rodgers' ultimatum or his decision to criticize McCarthy publicly days before a key game
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 26, 2026
                            
                    at
    1:04 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Steelers president Art Rooney II spent part of his Thanksgiving addressing his team's decision to bench, then release Aaron Rodgers following his actions with Mike McCarthy. McCarthy benched Rodgers after Rodgers gave him an ultimatum: relinquish play-calling duties or release him. The Steelers released Rodgers after he went scorched earth on McCarthy during a 35-minute interview on "The Pat McAfee Show." "I just want to say that I have 100% confidence in Mike McCarthy and I expect he'll be our coach this season, next season and beyond," Rooney told the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette. "The big thing, what happened this week, is insubordination can't be tolerated in any organization. When you start getting ultimatums, you can't live with that."  Rooney took issue with Rodgers' decision to publicly air his grievances with McCarthy, especially with the Steelers just days away from playing a big game against the Denver Broncos. "There's maybe a time and place after the season if he wanted to kind of unload," Rooney said. "He talks about wanting to be a good teammate, but you don't do that to your teammates a couple days before the game, that's for sure."  
Perhaps the most interesting thing Rooney said was regarding Pittsburgh's play-calling. "The sad thing is Mike took some of the bullets for Aaron in terms of some of the plays that were called, particularly in the red-zone troubles that we had," Rooney said. "Mike took some of the bullets for things that were going wrong down there. He tried to protect him, and it just wasn't working."One possible example of this may have been late in the first half of Pittsburgh's Week 8 win over the Browns. The Steelers were running at will, which made Pittsburgh's decision to call three straight passing plays inside Cleveland's 10-yard-line a head scratching decision to say the least. McCarthy accepted blame for those play calls when asked about them afterward. 
Regarding his team's future, Rooney said he is optimistic that Mason Rudolph can lead the Steelers' offense. Rudolph, a nine-year veteran who has 20 career starts under his belt, delivered for the Steelers when he was in a similar spot in 2023. When asked if he regrets his decision to bring Rodgers back, Rooney said he was disappointed with how things turned out. "We certainly had hopes that he would be successful here, and I thought at times we certainly got on a roll," he said. "We had high expectations.
"It's easy to say, knowing what I know today, what would I do? But we had a good experience last year, and so I kind of wasn't expecting it to go this way this year."

Legendary quarterbacks close out the holiday slate in one of the biggest games of the season

        The NFL's three-game Thanksgiving slate concludes with a blockbuster battle between two perennial playoff teams in the Buffalo Bills and Kansas City Chiefs. A pair of franchises that have regularly butted heads during the Josh Allen and Patrick Mahomes eras clash once again in one of the season's biggest showdowns to date.As is often the case when they square off in the regular season, there are significant postseason seeding implications at play in this showdown between the Bills and Chiefs. Buffalo stands in control of the AFC's No. 1 seed, while Kansas City is in a tightly contested race with the Denver Broncos for the AFC West crown and the top-four seed that comes with it. Should the Chiefs beat the Bills, not only would they solidify their standing in the division hunt, but they would also then give themselves a clear path to the top overall seed and a first-round bye.This game stands among the greatest Thanksgiving matchups in NFL history. The combined 17-3 record between the two teams is the second-best mark by win percentage entering a Thanksgiving game in the last 50 seasons.
Both sides are also playing their best football of the season heading into the holiday duel. This is just the second game in league history to feature two teams riding three-game win streaks in which all of those victories came by 17 or more points. The only other such instance came in 2007 between Tom Brady's New England Patriots and Peyton Manning's Indianapolis Colts. The quarterback face-off in this contest is about as legendary as that one.Where to watch Bills vs. Chiefs liveDate: Thursday, Nov. 26 | Time: 8:20 p.m. ETLocation: Highmark Stadium (Orchard Park, N.Y.)TV: NBC | Streaming: Fubo (try for free)Follow:  CBS Sports AppOdds: Bills -3, O/U 50.5 via DraftKings SportsbookBills vs. Chiefs key storylinesAnother Allen vs. Mahomes classic: A pair of all-time great quarterbacks have quite the history in head-to-head battles at this stage of their careers, and there is a sharp dichotomy between their records in regular-season matchups and playoff battles. While Allen owns a commanding 5-1 lead in the regular season, Mahomes has been dominant in win-or-go-home situations at 4-0. In games against each other, their passing numbers are nearly identical; Allen passed for 1,534 yards and 11 touchdowns to Mahomes' 1,552 yards and 10 touchdowns in their first 10 clashes. Where Allen owns a decided edge is in ball security (three interceptions vs. eight) and in rushing production (five touchdowns vs. zero).Top-tier running back showdown: Messaging out of Kansas City is that the Chiefs are hopeful Kenneth Walker III will return to action on Thursday following a two-game absence due to groin tightness. If he suits up, then the NFL is in for a tremendous running back battle. Walker (109.0) and Buffalo's James Cook III (106.0) rank second and third, respectively, in rushing yards per game and are in a race with Detroit Lions star Jahmyr Gibbs for the league rushing title. If Cook can return to the top of the leaderboard, he would pace the NFL in yardage for the second consecutive year. On Sunday, he set a new record for the most consecutive games (nine) with at least 75 rushing yards and a rushing touchdown in a season.Bills defense levels up: Over the first six games of the season, the Bills had to post gaudy scoring numbers in order to make up for a leaky defense. That was not the case in any of their last four games. All of a sudden, this unit ranks 11th in EPA per play allowed, has not surrendered more than 12 points in a game since Oct. 18 and is no longer a liability but rather an asset. Defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard's unit has gone 15 quarters without allowing a touchdown, which is the NFL's longest single-season streak since 2000. The group still has to prove that it can play at this level against more formidable competition, though.Chiefs ride historic hot streak: Just like their upcoming opponent, the Chiefs enjoyed a stretch of games against lesser competition heading into the Thanksgiving battle and took care of business with ease. In routs of the New York Jets, Atlanta Falcons and Arizona Cardinals, the Chiefs tied the longest streak in franchise history of wins by at least 21 points (three). Even dating back to their last loss, Mahomes is in the midst of a scalding stretch with 13 passing touchdowns and no interceptions.Bills vs. Chiefs predictionIt is difficult to knock Kansas City, because when it wins, it does so in resounding fashion and shows all the makings of a future Super Bowl winner. But the Chiefs' strength of schedule and results against projected playoff teams do raise questions about whether they can take down the Bills on the road in primetime. The Chiefs have only played three games against opponents with winning records all season and are just 1-2 in those contests. Both losses came on the road. Simply put, they have not shown an ability to win games like the one they are about to walk into.
At the same time, the Bills defeated each of the three best teams on their schedule thus far. Plus, for whatever reason, Allen has Mahomes' number when they meet in the regular season. Add the defensive revival into the equation, and everything comes up Bills in this matchup. Pick: Bills 38, Chiefs 33

The league is trying to take over nearly the entire week. The holiday slate of games kicked off on Wednesday night with the Rams beating the Packers 26-13 in the NFL's first-ever Thanksgiving Eve game. Hopefully you enjoyed the NFL's newest tradition, because it will be sticking around. The league is planning on making this game an annual event. The game between the Rams and Packers served as the appetizer for a wild day for games on Thanksgiving. The Turkey Day action started in Detroit, where the Bears pulled off a dramatic 39-35 win in a game where Caleb Williams threw a touchdown pass to Rome Odunze with just three seconds left to help Chicago stun Detroit. The two teams combined for 1,007 yards of offense, which is the second-most ever in a Thanksgiving game. 
The game in Detroit was crazy, but the second game of the day in Dallas might have topped it with the Cowboys blowing a 31-10 lead in a 39-38 loss to the Eagles. It was the largest blown lead on Thanksgiving in NFL history. It also made the Cowboys the first team in NFL history to lose two different games at home in a single season where they blew a 14-point lead or more in the fourth quarter. The Turkey Day nightcap will be taking place in Buffalo, and it's definitely the main event of the day: It's Patrick Mahomes facing off against Josh Allen for the 11th time. The rivalry between USC and UCLA took an odd turn off the field

        The rivalry between USC and UCLA is already heated enough on the field, but it doesn't always stay within the lines. The USC band pranked the Bruins this week, and now it will pay the price.This week, members of the Trojan Marching Band tampered with the sign on the Wasserman Football Center, turning it into "Ass Football Center." Photos of the prank went viral, and USC president Beong-Soo Kim stepped in to discipline the entire band.In a statement released on Wednesday night, Kim apologized to UCLA and announced his decision to bar the USC band from performing at the Rose Bowl this weekend.
"Out of respect for UCLA, and to provide time to reflect on the collective responsibility we share to uphold our university's values, the university and the Trojan Marching Band's leadership have decided that the band will not take the field for their traditional pre-game and halftime performances at the Rose Bowl on Saturday," Kim said in a statement.
Perhaps this prank highlights just how important the game is to both sides this season. It's the first time since 2005 that the Trojans (8-3) and Bruins (10-1) are ranked inside the top 25. Both are also still alive for a spot in the Big Ten Championship Game, and UCLA is clinging to a spot in the College Football Playoff.
The Bruins will be looking for revenge on Saturday — both because of this prank and as they look to end a two-game losing streak to their cross-town rival. This top-15 matchup kicks off at 3:30 p.m.  ET on Saturday, and you can catch all the action on CBS and Paramount+ Premium.

title: What all 32 NFL teams should be thankful for this Thanksgiving - CBS Sports
description: On an electric NFL Thanksgiving, I brought together my fellow CBS Sports writers Bryan DeArdo, Jordan Dajani, Carter Bahns and Garrett P
body:
On an electric NFL Thanksgiving, I brought together my fellow CBS Sports writers Bryan DeArdo, Jordan Dajani, Carter Bahns and Garrett Podell to find one thing each team can be thankful for this holiday season.  The gap between the best team and the worst team in the NFL is quite large, but even though not all teams have the playoffs in their future, or even a winning record, they can still be thankful for what they do have,Thanksgiving offers a natural opportunity to take stock of the good things, even during an NFL season that has not gone according to plan for every team. Some franchises enter the holiday firmly in the Super Bowl race, while others are already measuring progress through young players, improved units and the draft capital that could shape a brighter future.AFC EastWriter: Shanna McCarriston
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Bills (9-1)Winning despite turnovers – The Bills have a lot of reasons for gratitude. This one is somewhat of a good news, bad news situation: the team is turning the ball over more than they should, but they are still getting wins. It just goes to show that great teams will find ways to win games regardless. Josh Allen, James Cook, and their record are the obvious things they should be thankful for, but this one is most interesting to me because, as a team that has turned the ball over twice in three of the last four games and five times in a single game this season, 9-1 is impressive. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Patriots (5-5)Drake Maye value – The Patriots have had a difficult season in terms of injuries, so much so that they're running out of spots on IR, and on-field struggles even when healthy. Quarterback Drake Maye is out for an extended period of time, likely the rest of the season, and without him the offense fell flat. The team still had their fair share of struggles with Maye, don't get me wrong, but if him being sidelined proved anything, it's how valuable he is to the team. In a season where many were questioning his real impact, wondering if last year was a fluke, the team can be grateful that when they do get Maye back (even if it's next year), the offense will be bumped back up.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Jets (3-8)Pass defense – The Jets are another team far outside the playoff race, but it's not all bad! Heading into Week 11, the Jets pass defense was fifth-best in the league, allowing 196.8 yards per game through 10 weeks. This alone won't get them to a Super Bowl, but on a team with many issues to point to, they can be thankful that something is working. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Dolphins (1-9)Forcing turnovers – Looking at the Dolphins record, it can be hard to think that they have anything to be thankful for. A high draft pick is one thing they can be grateful for, but so is their defense. They were tied for fifth-most interceptions with nine through 10 weeks and added two more against the Bills last week. The run defense had the challenge of facing Jonathan Taylor, Jahmyr Gibbs and James Cook and held them to under 100 yards each. 
AFC NorthWriter: Bryan DeArdo
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Bengals (7-3)Joe Burrow — Cincinnati boasts a reinvigorated defense (led by Dexter Lawrence) and the best receiving duo in the NFL in Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins. Burrow, however, remains the key to the Bengals' success. He's currently on pace to become the first player in history to throw for 5,000 yards and 50 touchdowns in a season while also completing at least 70% of his passes. He's among the MVP front-runners.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Browns (6-4)Todd Monken — With respect to John Harbaugh, Monken should win NFL Coach of the Year if the Browns continue to win. Cleveland is 6-4 and would be in the playoffs if the postseason started today. Monken has revived Deshaun Watson's career.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Steelers (6-4)Jaylen Warren — Warren was arguably the biggest reason for Pittsburgh's 6-2 start. The former undrafted rookie rushed for over 700 yards over that span that included four 100-yard games. Warren and the Steelers' offense have fallen off in recent weeks, though. Warren becomes even more valuable within the offense as the Aaron Rodgers drama sparked a quarterback change.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Ravens (4-7)Derrick Henry — While it's been a lost season in Baltimore, Ravens fans still get a chance to watch an all-time great do his thing. Henry is still playing well and setting new milestones in his 11th NFL season. This season, he's moved into third all-time in rushing touchdowns and seventh in career rushing yards.AFC SouthWriter: Jordan Dajani Jaguars (7-3)
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Liam Coen – The Jaguars are now 20-7 under coach Liam Coen, who has turned this franchise from an afterthought to a Super Bowl contender. Coen has Trevor Lawrence finally living up to the lofty expectations set before him as a prospect coming out of Clemson, and has put together an impressive staff that includes defensive coordinator Anthony Campanile and offensive coordinator Grant Udinski. Both could be head coaches next year.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Texans (4-6)C.J. Stroud – Imagine how disappointing the Texans would be this year if it weren't for the play of C.J. Stroud? He's thrown three touchdowns in three straight games, and scored at least two touchdowns in seven straight games. That's the longest such streak in franchise history. Stroud has thrown 22 touchdowns compared to just four interceptions this season. We no longer have to wonder if the Texans have a franchise quarterback.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Colts (3-8)The season is almost over – There are just six games remaining in the regular season. That's good news for Colts fans.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Titans (1-9)Future drafts – The one-win Titans traded away star defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons and safety Amani Hooker for some nice draft capital. Tennessee now holds four first-round picks and three second-round picks in the next two drafts, which could expedite a seemingly never-ending rebuild. As long as Mike Borgonzi doesn't draft another developmental pass rusher.AFC WestWriter: Shanna McCarriston
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Chiefs (8-2)Patrick Mahomes back on top – The Chiefs are back and so is Patrick Mahomes. Kansas City's woes of last season are over, and the fans can breathe a sigh of relief that last year was a fluke. Mahomes has 22 touchdowns with just four interceptions this year, along with 2,709 yards. He is looking like the Super Bowl contender he has been in the past, and his offense has fixed many of the mistakes they had last season. With Mahomes playing like he is, this team has a real chance of going all the way. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Broncos (8-2)Division still in reach – Last season the Broncos won the division, but that was with the Chiefs struggling. This year, K.C. is among the top in the league and Denver is still within reach of the divisional title. That is a major accomplishment for Sean Payton's squad. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Raiders (4-7)Mendoza Era begins – The Raiders season has been filled with ups and downs. It started off strong, but then took a turn. The hope the Raiders and their fans can have is that the Fernando Mendoza era has begun and they can start to get excited about who they anticipate to be their franchise guy. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Chargers (1-9)High draft pick – The Chargers season hasn't been what they hoped, leaving lots of questions about their quarterback and coach. The good news is that they will be getting a high draft pick this year. Now they just need to do something with it. 
NFC EastWriter: Garrett Podell
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Giants (6-3-1)John Harbaugh -- The New York Giants are fresh off a 23-18 win over the AFC South-leading Jacksonville Jaguars (7-3) in Week 11 that has the Giants out to a two-game lead in the NFC East over the Cowboys. New coach John Harbaugh is pushing all the right buttons and has the Giants tracking toward a division title despite Jaxson Dart and Brian Burns suffering season-ending injuries within the first three weeks of the 2026 season. He is certainly someone the Giants are grateful to have leading their football team. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Cowboys (5-6)Dak Prescott -- Prescott is dragging his 29th-ranked scoring defense (28.4 points per game allowed) into the NFC East division race by powering the league's No. 4 scoring offense (30.6 points per game). Prescott became the fourth player in NFL history with 300-plus passing yards and five-plus total touchdowns in consecutive games across Weeks 10 and 11, per CBS Sports Research. He joined Daunte Culpepper (2004), Tom Brady (2007) and Ben Roethlisberger (2014) in this exclusive club. 
Prescott now ranks second in the NFL in passing yards (3,049) and second in passing touchdowns (25) while ranking eighth in passer rating (101.0) and fourth in expected points added (EPA) per dropback (0.21). He is pulling off one of the NFL's biggest carry jobs this season, and he is someone that owner/general manager Jerry Jones should be eternally grateful to have leading his football team. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Commanders (4-5-1)Jayden Daniels -- Daniels looks like his 2024 NFL Offensive Rookie of the Year self with all of his tools available to him. Daniels finished with 289 passing yards on 23 of 35 attempts while leading the Commanders with 55 yards rushing in a 22-20, buzzer-beating victory over the AFC North-leading Cincinnati Bengals. Washington now has consecutive wins over two first-place teams, the Giants and Bengals, no less, for the first time since the 2024 season, when Daniels won Offensive Rookie of the Year honors and the Commanders reached the NFC Championship Game.After tossing a 32-yard game-winning touchdown to Stefon Diggs to shock the Giants and then the game-winning drive on Monday against the AFC North-leading Bengals, it's clear Daniels has his magic back.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Eagles (3-7)Saquon Barkley -- The 2024 NFL Offensive Player of the Year running back powered the Philadelphia Eagles (75 rushing yards, including a 38-yard rushing touchdown, on 17 carries) to a 19-16 upset victory of the Pittsburgh Steelers to end the franchise's seven-game winning streak. Barkley is currently on a streak of four consecutive games with a rushing touchdown, the longest streak of his career in a lost year for his franchise. NFC NorthWriter: Garrett Podell
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Lions (8-2)Jahmyr Gibbs -- Gibbs leads the entire NFL in rushing yards (1,098), scrimmage yards (1,502) and touchdowns from scrimmage (15) through the first 11 weeks of the 2026 season. Gibbs is now the first player with 1,500-plus scrimmage yards and 15-plus scrimmage touchdowns through the first 10 games of a season since Emmitt Smith accomplished the feat in 1995.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Bears (8-2)Jeffery Simmons -- The Chicago Bears needed a game-changing presence along their defensive line, and All-Pro defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons has been just that in his first three games. He racked up 3.0 sacks in Chicago's 21-13 Week 11 win over the New Orleans Saints, so Simmons is now up to 5.0 sacks and three consecutive wins in his three-game Bears career. Despite playing just three games with the Bears since coming over in a trade with the Tennessee Titans, he now co-leads his new team in sacks (5.0) with Austin Booker, who has played in all 10 games for Chicago this season. Simmons is now the only player in NFL history with five-plus sacks and three wins in his first three games after switching teams during a season,  according to CBS Sports Research.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Vikings (7-3)Kirk Cousins -- Yes, the Minnesota Vikings are fresh off being steamrolled 35-10 on "Sunday Night Football" against the top-seeded San Francisco 49ers (9-1), but Kirk Cousins stabilizes their offense in a way Kyler Murray and Carson Wentz could not. He helped lead them to a 30-10 victory at the Green Bay Packers in Week 10 by doing just enough. Minnesota is in the NFC North division title race going forward because Cousins is a Viking once again. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Packers (6-5)Jordan Love -- Yes, the Green Bay Packers' patchwork offensive line didn't give Jordan Love (220 yards passing, one touchdown, one interception on 17-of-27 passing) a chance against Brian Flores' No. 1 Vikings defense in Week 10 in a 30-10 defeat at Lambeau Field. He was sacked eight times, tied for the most in a single game this season with Deshaun Watson (twice) and Justin Herbert. Love made some strong throws when he had the time. NFC SouthWriter: Carter Bahns
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Panthers (5-5)A weak division – There has been no greater beneficiary of the NFC South's ineptitude since the start of 2025 than the Panthers. They won the division with a losing record last season and -- with their first-place standing at just 5-5 -- are on track to do so again in 2026.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Buccaneers (3-7)Defensive improvement – For all the love the Vikings and Seahawks receive for their vicious defenses, it is actually the Buccaneers who lead the NFL in EPA per play allowed. Tampa Bay's unit has only gotten better as the season progresses and is on a new level right now, having forced at least four turnovers in each of the last three games. It also completed the only shutout of the season in Week 8.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Falcons (3-7)Three optimism-inspiring wins – The losses have been bad. There is no way around that. But conversely, each of Atlanta's three wins is as stellar as the losses are concerning. The Falcons handed the Packers their worst loss of the year. They demolished the Saints for their only divisional victory. And they are responsible for the only blemish on the 49ers' resume. The lows might be low, but the highs prove that Atlanta can hang with anyone.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Saints (3-7)Jordyn Tyson's arrival from injured reserve – After he spent the first eight weeks of his career on IR, the No. 8 overall pick displayed all kinds of promise in two healthy games. He racked up 11 catches on 13 targets in his second outing, which is a massive workload for a rookie with only eight quarters of experience and one that suggests he could carry this offense if he stays in the lineup over the next month and a half.NFC WestWriter: Carter Bahns
                            
    
                                                
                    
    49ers (9-1)Brock Purdy's career year – It will be difficult to outpace Joe Burrow in the MVP race, but Purdy is in the conversation. He was the catalyst behind the 49ers' stupendous first half of the season and is now the NFL's all-time leader in career passer rating, success rate and adjusted yards per attempt. Not bad for a former Mr. Irrelevant. Most impressive is that he is playing his best football while dealing with a plethora of injuries at wide receiver.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Seahawks (6-4)Quarterback depth – That Mike Macdonald had to assert that Sam Darnold is the team's starter when healthy is a testament more to Drew Lock playing up than Darnold playing down. Lock is 3-0 as a starter and won the season opener after taking over in the first quarter. To have someone capable of not only keeping the offense afloat when the starter is hurt but to thrive with a 125.6 passer rating is a major reason why Seattle is still in the postseason hunt.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Rams (7-4)Strength of schedule regression – If not for the highly manageable slate the Rams faced from Weeks 7-10, the conversation around Los Angeles would reek even more of disappointment than it already does. The combined records of the last four teams they played: 11-26-1. That was strong medicine for a preseason Super Bowl favorite that stunningly opened the year at 2-4.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Cardinals (3-8)Trey McBride – At least the Cardinals have a building block to construct a foundation around as they embark on their rebuild. Since Jeremiyah Love's rookie year has been a complete injury-riddled disappointment and the wide receiver group is torn down to the studs, it is a good thing McBride is around to provide some semblance of life on a team whose season is headed down the drain.

But the path is clear: Win and they're in both the Big Ten Championship and likely the playoff. But can they do it as a one-touchdown underdog with potentially the third-string quarterback leading the offense?We'll find out this final weekend of the regular season, when rivalries can throw everything out of sorts.The biggest games are in the Big Ten, where the championship race still involves six teams, but the roads could run through Eugene, Oregon, and Iowa City. No. 12 Oregon hosts No. 24 Washington, and No. 13 Iowa hosts No. 25 Nebraska.
The Hawkeyes have five different ways into the Big Ten title game (all require a win), and Oregon has eight possibilities, including four with a loss. Only UCLA controls its own destiny with a win.Yeah, it's wild.Meanwhile, three teams are vying to face Georgia in the SEC Championship: No. 3 Texas, No. 6 Alabama and No. 5 Tennessee. The Vols' path is the simplest: a win against Vanderbilt and a loss by Texas at Texas A&M.In the Big 12, No. 11 Texas Tech can punch its ticket to the Big 12 title game with a win against TCU. Utah awaits.
So, read up on the conference tiebreakers and check out our experts' picks for the biggest games in the final week of the regular season.Nebraska vs. No. 13 Iowa Friday -- Noon on CBS CBSSports.com, CBS Sports App Paramount+ Premium: When it comes to rivalry games, I'm never as excited to bet spreads because things get a little weird. That weirdness often bleeds into the way points are scored too. In rivalries, you suddenly see teams that can't score putting points up in a hurry, and the other way around. So I'm avoiding all of that and sticking to the basics here. Nebraska is coming off a huge win last week. Even with this being a rivalry game, there could be an emotional letdown. Meanwhile, we've gone over what's at stake for the Hawkeyes. Give me the Iowa moneyline. Pick: Iowa (-200) -- Tom Fornelli
